title: Research and entity deadlines
instructions: A client asks about revoking an S election and about filing deadlines for several related entities.

exhibits.title: Client question
exhibits.content: Maple, Inc., a calendar-year S corporation, wants to revoke its S election effective January 1, 2025. Shareholders owning 70% of the stock sign the revocation on **February 20, 2025** and don't specify an effective date.

exhibits.title: Related entities (calendar year, 2025 returns, no extensions)
exhibits.content:
- The Maple Family Trust (complex trust)
- Maple Foundation (§501(c)(3) public charity; gross receipts $900,000)
- Maple Ventures LLC (three members; no election)
- Maple Holdings, Inc. (C corporation)

parts.prompt: Which excerpt (paraphrased for study) determines when Maple's revocation takes effect?

excerpts.text: An election may be made for a tax year at any time during the preceding tax year or on or before the 15th day of the 3rd month of the tax year.

A revocation made on or before the 15th day of the 3rd month of the tax year is effective on the first day of that year; a later revocation is effective on the first day of the following year, unless the revocation specifies a prospective date.

An election terminates if the corporation has accumulated earnings and profits at the close of each of 3 consecutive years and passive investment income exceeds 25% of gross receipts in each of those years.
Distributions by an S corporation with accumulated earnings and profits are applied first against the accumulated adjustments account, then against earnings and profits.

parts.explanation: The revocation was made by the 15th day of the 3rd month and has majority consent, so it is effective January 1, 2025 under §1362(d)(1)(C).

parts.prompt: Original due dates for the 2025 returns.

rows.label: Maple Ventures LLC — Form 1065
rows.explanation: 15th day of the 3rd month (March 15 is a Sunday).

rows.label: Consent needed to revoke an S election
